correctness.rationale: Expansion of the full finite powered-distance quadratic form is exact; within-blade Cauchy–Schwarz and weighted Cauchy–Schwarz are simultaneously sharp. Strict scalar monotonicity locates precisely one threshold; null-vector equality conditions give dimension. An independent full-matrix Jacobi eigensolver checked 131 blade vectors, plus all strict balanced/unbalanced integer endpoints. All all-size conclusions follow from symbolic inequalities, not enumeration.

originality.rationale: A located 2011 conference report explicitly states a generalized-roundness formula for classical equal-blade windmills, so that homogeneous formula is treated as prior art. The accepted contribution is instead the full heterogeneous-blade scalar criterion together with the strict Schur-majorization law, two fixed-budget unique extremizers, and critical eigenspace/dimension. Sources inspected do not state these mixed-size comparisons; important unavailable manuscripts are named as risks.
residual_risks: Original unpublished Cornell 2011 manuscript could include heterogeneous blades or rearrangement comparisons; only conference abstracts were accessible.
The 1990 Deza–Maehara text was not accessible, so a stronger original implication cannot be ruled out.
Other older graph-metric generalized-roundness work may be unindexed; database search is not a proof of uniqueness.

value.rationale: Determining how clique-size allocation changes generalized roundness at fixed vertex and blade budgets is a natural metric embedding design problem. The strict majorization order classifies all allocations, identifies unique best and worst geometries, and supplies exact Hilbert snowflake dimensional transitions. This is not a renamed known homogeneous formula or an arbitrary finite numerical slice.
